articleHeader.title: What is J2EE (Java 2 Enterprise Edition)?
articleHeader.subtitle: A complete beginner-friendly guide to J2EE covering Servlets, JSP, JDBC, MVC architecture, enterprise applications, application servers, and modern Jakarta EE.

blocks.text: J2EE (Java 2 Enterprise Edition) is a platform used for developing large-scale, distributed, enterprise-level Java applications. It provides APIs and technologies such as Servlets, JSP, JDBC, EJB, JMS, and Web Services to build secure, scalable, and multi-tier applications.
J2EE was developed by Sun Microsystems and later maintained by Oracle Corporation. Today, J2EE is known as Jakarta EE after being transferred to the Eclipse Foundation.

J2EE is mainly used in banking systems, e-commerce platforms, ERP systems, healthcare applications, enterprise dashboards, and government applications where reliability, scalability, and security are extremely important.

items.text: — J2EE introduced by Sun Microsystems.
— J2EE renamed to Java EE.
— Oracle transferred Java EE to Eclipse Foundation.
— Java EE officially became Jakarta EE.
— Jakarta EE widely used for cloud-native enterprise Java applications.

items.title: Enterprise Level
items.text: Designed for large-scale enterprise applications with high reliability and scalability.

items.title: Web Development
items.text: Supports Servlets, JSP, and web technologies for building dynamic web applications.

items.title: Database Connectivity
items.text: JDBC API allows applications to connect with MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, and other databases.

items.title: Security
items.text: Provides authentication, authorization, role-based access control, and secure enterprise APIs.

items.title: Scalable
items.text: Applications can handle thousands or millions of users efficiently.

items.title: Distributed Computing
items.text: Supports distributed applications across multiple servers.

items.title: Reusable Components
items.text: Enterprise Beans and modular architecture improve code reusability.

items.title: Platform Independent
items.text: Runs on any operating system that supports JVM.

blocks.text: J2EE follows a multi-tier architecture that separates presentation, business logic, and database layers.

items.text: — Java technology used to create dynamic web applications.
— Used for creating dynamic web pages with HTML + Java.
— Java Database Connectivity API used to connect databases.
— Enterprise JavaBeans used for enterprise business logic.
— Java Messaging Service used for asynchronous messaging.
— Java Persistence API used for ORM and database operations.
— SOAP and REST APIs for communication between applications.

items.a: J2EE is a Java platform for building enterprise-level distributed applications using technologies like Servlet, JSP, JDBC, and EJB.

items.q: Q2. What is the difference between J2SE and J2EE?
items.a: J2SE is used for standalone applications while J2EE is used for enterprise web applications.
Servlet is a Java technology used to create dynamic web applications and handle client requests.
JSP (JavaServer Pages) is used to create dynamic web pages using HTML and Java code.
JDBC is an API that connects Java applications with databases.

blocks.text: J2EE is one of the most important enterprise Java technologies ever created. It laid the foundation for modern enterprise web development and introduced standards that are still used today in Jakarta EE and modern Java frameworks.
If you want to become a Java backend developer or work on enterprise applications, learning J2EE concepts like Servlets, JSP, JDBC, MVC architecture, and application servers is extremely valuable.

items.a: Yes. J2EE evolved into Jakarta EE and is still widely used in enterprise Java development.

items.q: What is the difference between Java EE and Jakarta EE?
items.a: Java EE was managed by Oracle, while Jakarta EE is managed by the Eclipse Foundation.
Spring Boot is more popular for modern Java applications, but J2EE concepts are still foundational for enterprise development.

items.q: Which server is used in J2EE?
items.a: Popular servers include Apache Tomcat, GlassFish, WildFly, WebLogic, and WebSphere.
